rationale: PLAN_DATA_LAYER 4: a table stored with its breakpoint order swapped (a transposed CXT): the values are laid out first-breakpoint-fastest instead of the DAVE-ML last-breakpoint-fastest, with the shape kept, so every 2-D table (CXT, CMT, CLT, ..., T_MIL) is scrambled while the 1-D tables are unchanged.

PLAN_DATA_LAYER 4: a breakpoint name mapped to the wrong input (alpha <-> el): CXT's breakpoints are named {alpha, el} while the data are indexed (el, alpha), so a lookup by name and the build-up read the wrong input.
PLAN_DATA_LAYER 4: a unit not converted (ft2 kept as m2): S = 300 'm2' instead of 27.87 m2 changes every aero load of the model built from the data.

PLAN_DATA_LAYER 4: provenance stripped from one table (the last table of each file loses its source, e.g. dcndr, T_MAX): the object would carry a number without a source; validation must refuse it (vital:data:noProvenance).
PLAN_DATA_LAYER 4: JSON written with num2str (4 decimals / 5 significant digits): the save/load round trip loses precision (e.g. 11.32 * 0.3048, 1/3, the 0.1-type table values).
PLAN_DATA_LAYER 4: fromData takes the CG from the wrong axis (the MRC, 0.10 cbar = 0.345 m aft of the 25 % CG): the weight acts at the wrong point and the pitching moment about the CG changes.
Criterion 7: the SHA-256 check against data/MANIFEST.json skipped: a changed NASA file would be read without notice.

pattern: if isfinite(P.minValue(j)), x = max(x, P.minValue(j)); end
rationale: The data object's build-up forgets the DAVE-ML minValue saturation (ADR-014; e.g. vt >= 0.1 ft/s in F16_aero.dml): it no longer equals the generated runtime code bit for bit.
The expression whitelist bypassed: a .vital.json file could make MATLAB call any function (e.g. system) when it is loaded; data must never be code.
